title: 'Some think endometriosis is just a bad period, but it's so much worse'

input.lead: Women with endometriosis are suffering financially as well as physically, a new report by MPs warns
input.summary: Women with endometriosis are suffering financially as well as physically, a new report by MPs warns
input.evidence_text: 'Some think endometriosis is just a bad period, but it's so much worse' - BBC News Image source, Chloe Ward Image caption, Chloe Ward says years of treatment, surgery and time off work have left her paying a heavy financial price for endometriosis By James Fell and Mat Trewern , North West Published 1 hour ago Women with endometriosis are being forced out of work, losing income and facing significant financial hardship because of the condition, according to a new report by MPs. The inquiry by the All-Party Parliamentary Group on Endometriosis, supported by Endometriosis UK, found 47% of women with the condition had lost income because of their symptoms, while 28% had left a job altogether. Among them was Chloe Ward, from Bolton, who said her endometriosis - which can cause severe pain, fatigue, heavy bleeding and fertility problems - had cost her thousands of pounds and affected her ability to run her own business. She said: "A lot of people think it's just a bad period, but it's so much worse." About one in 10 women suffer from the condition, but diagnosis can be a lengthy process. Chloe said it took seven years for her to be diagnosed. She said being self-employed in the beauty industry meant she had flexibility, but no financial safety net. "If I'm not there to do the treatments, nobody pays me," she said. She told BBC Radio Manchester she had lost clients over the years because flare-ups could leave her unable to work at short notice. Image source, Chloe Ward Image caption, Endo the Night encourages people to host fundraising events while raising awareness of endometriosis Chloe is now waiting for a hysterectomy, which will mean more time away from work. "There's so much to it that people don't understand," she said. The financial impact has extended beyond lost ear

title: HMOs 'targeted' as 25 incidents of vandalism in Salford linked

input.lead: Officers believe HMOs and properties mistaken for HMOs are being "targeted" in Salford
input.summary: Officers believe HMOs and properties mistaken for HMOs are being "targeted" in Salford
input.evidence_text: HMOs 'targeted' as 25 incidents of vandalism in Salford linked - BBC News Image caption, Police say HMOs and houses mistaken as HMOs are being vandalised across Salford By James Fell North West Published 14 October 2026 Police are investigating 25 linked incidents of criminal damage across Salford and believe houses in multiple occupation (HMOs) are being targeted. The incidents, including smashed windows, vandalism and graffiti, have been reported since 5 October and each incident follows a similar pattern of offending, Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said. The force said the attacks on homes were in different parts of the city but they were currently being treated as linked. The most recent incident was reported on Tuesday evening. Ch Insp Lee Gridley said inquiries so far had led officers to believe "HMOs, and properties that have been mistaken for HMOs, are being targeted". "No one should be made to feel unsafe in their own home and it's not something that will be tolerated in Salford, or anywhere in Greater Manchester," he said. Officers will be carrying out patrols across Salford throughout the week while investigations continue. Detectives are trawling through CCTV and monitoring social media coverage of the incidents. A 13-year-old boy who was arrested as part of an investigation on 8 October has been released on police bail. GMP is urging anyone with information or footage to come forward. Patsy McKie's youngest son Dorrie, 20, was shot dead in the Hulme area of Manchester in 1999. Just days later, she co-founded Mothers Against Violence (MAVUK) and dedicated the rest of her life to travelling across the world to raise awareness of her anti-crime campaign. A colourful mural, created by artist Marcus Lane, has been painted at the MAVUK Hulme Centre following her death in January 2025 at the age of 77. Image caption, Patsy McKie set up Mothers Against Violence days after her son was shot dead in 1999 "She was a very bright person, even through some of the most difficult periods of her life," said her son, Ian Swanston. "She wanted to bring a sense of colour to the world. "A creative artwork representing Patsy would have to be colourful, because that's definitely what she wants." Dorrie has been about to start a sports and leisure course at college when he was shot dead amid spiralling gang violence in Manchester. Patsy believed deeply in the strength of community and in the possibility of healing, even during the most difficult of times. "She always said that if young people are doing something positive, they won't have time to do the things that are negative in our community," said Ian. "So she really wanted to be able to create spaces that allowed young people to excel." title: Is the funding market getting harder and what could that mean for Manchester? | Manchester Digital

input.lead: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing.
input.summary: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised
input.evidence_text: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised. More capital is being concentrated in fewer companies while the market for exits remains difficult Financial news recently added another dimension to that discussion. AI-related shares fell last week after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slower approach to the development of increasingly capable AI models. Nvidia finished the day down 3.4%, SoftBank fell 10.7% in Tokyo Additionally, the Bank of England is predicted to increase interest rates later this year, which could affect the North West's tech funding landscape by raising the cost of capital across the board, compressing valuations, pushing investors toward profitability over growth-at-all The British Business Bank's 2026 Small Business Equity Tracker found that equity investment into UK smaller businesses fell 4% to £12.3bn in 2025. Seed deal numbers fell 27% and venture deals fell 13%. AI companies attracted 44% of all investment into smaller businesses while the Beauhurst recorded £14.4bn of UK equity investment across 2,799 deals in the first half of 2026 but three AI companies accounted for 29% of all the capital raised. Those very large rounds can make the overall market look stronger than it feels to businesses raising at seed or Ser Beauhurst's analysis shows that UK equity investment more than doubled between 2017 and 2021 to £32.2bn while annual exits remained at around 400 to 500. An exit takes a median of four years from a funding round

input.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained.
